crime: Every evening, one girl told a story by the lounge fireplace. {WITCH_NAME} listened from the back and never offered one.

One night the storyteller found her alone in the courtyard, looking up. "What do you see?" {WITCH_NAME} took her hand, and her Magic gave the girl a night from her childhood: lying on a roof, counting forty meteors. The girl lay back on the fountain rim. "Go on in. I'll watch for them a bit longer."

The next evening, the storyteller told the meteor night by the fire as her own. She tossed dry leaves in; sparks rained onto her right cuff, and she patted them out, laughing. "That night was mine," {WITCH_NAME} said. The girl laughed. "I lived it too. It's mine now." The room laughed along.
As a child, {WITCH_NAME} had heard her sister tell the family about the meteor night at supper as her own. When she said it was hers, they laughed. "You never say anything."
That evening she followed the storyteller out. As the girl lay on the fountain rim watching for falling stars, {WITCH_NAME} closed her hands on her throat until she stopped moving.
About ten minutes later she came back and sat among the prisoners by the fire, in their sight until lockup.

In the trial court, she touched each prisoner's hand and gave them her memory of the fountain: the storyteller alive, squeezing her hand. "Go on in. I'll watch for them a bit longer." So the prisoners ruled that she had left the girl alive and someone else killed her while {WITCH_NAME} sat with them.

Then a prisoner touched the dead girl's right cuff and found a burn hole. In the memory, {WITCH_NAME}'s fingers rested on that spot, and the cloth was intact. The memory was from the night before the sparks; when {WITCH_NAME} came back to the fire, the girl was already dead.
fields.epitaph: All she wanted was for one girl to see her stars, and she could not bear it when one did.
fields.epithet: The Stargazer Whose Nights Others Told
execution: The execution stand raises an iron rooftop beneath a vault hung with forty spiked iron stars. She lies chained to it on her back, face up.
An iron girl sits at the edge of the roof and tells the meteor night as her own. "I lay on a roof and counted forty fall."
Then the iron girl counts. At each number, a star drops from the vault onto the girl chained below: the first onto her chest, the rest across her body, one by one.
At forty, the iron girl bows to a clatter of iron applause. Beneath the fallen stars, the chained girl lies still.

magic.name: Through My Eyes
magic.text: With a touch, she lets someone relive one of her memories as her: every sight, sound and feeling.
